title: migrate: record a body checksum in the ledger and refuse an applied migration whose SQL changed

basis: D25; #616 (the offline limit stated); the ledger identity rule's own tolerance for a fifth column; Prisma checksum / Drizzle hash precedent
decisions.title: The ledger records a body checksum; migrate refuses an applied migration whose body changed; status reports it
the banner boundary, the normalization and the checksum's stored form
the working-directory pattern: one cd per call, never a persistent one
the banner literal stays local to the ledger; the live witness is its drift detector
test fakes that identify statements by prefix gain one alter-table branch; production is untouched
the checksum argument is required; a fake that only lacks the new column changes minimally
a raised file is hashed whole, banner or not
a file that fails only because it lacks the new field or argument gains exactly that
apply-migration-body-changed: every changed file, abbreviated checksums, one pure comparison shared by migrate and status
a run with nothing pending compares nothing; status is where a changed body is reported
status compares bodies on a run with no disagreement; a disagreement is reported alone, as today
the planner decides non-contract questions on the spot; instructions carry both branches
an old ledger is read through a four-column fallback and upgraded by the first command that writes
apply-ledger-filtered: judged where identity is judged, catalog read only on detection, the message names state, role and policies
